newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB writes to treasurer on big-bank mergers.
newsitem.headline: NAB writes to treasurer on big-bank mergers.

text.p: Australia's biggest bank, National Australia Bank, has written to Treasurer Peter Costello to protest against a government freeze on big-bank mergers.
NAB managing director Don Argus wrote to Costello about 10 days after the treasurer last month announced the ban on mergers between the four big domestic banks, NAB spokesman Haydn Park said.
Park declined on Wednesday to release a copy of the letter.
"You would have to consider that private correspondence," he said.
But the letter largely reflected the comments Argus made last week at the bank's half-year profit briefing, Park added.
Argus said in the briefing that Canberra's freeze on mergers had made NAB and the other three big local banks vulnerable to foreign takeover.
The government has said competition in the banking sector must spread and deepen before it would sanction a major bank merger.
Argus last week criticised the government's stance, arguing that competition was intense and warning this was beginning to hamper profit growth.
The other three major domestic banks are Westpac Banking Corp, Commonwealth Bank of Australia and the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd.
